name: mzML Spectrum Viewer & MS/MS Annotator
tagline: Open mzML or MGF files in your browser, average scans, measure peak gaps, and annotate fragments of linear or cyclic peptides.
description: Load an mzML or MGF file directly from your computer (nothing is uploaded), browse scans, average the scans of a precursor, and annotate the MS/MS spectrum against a linear or head-to-tail cyclic peptide. Measure the distance between two peaks to get residue, dipeptide and neutral-loss suggestions, accept or override every assignment, and export the annotated spectrum, structure and peak table.

inputs.name: file
inputs.label: Spectrum file (mzML or MGF)
inputs.help: mzML (plain or indexed; zlib, MS-Numpress, 32/64-bit) or MGF. The file is read inside your browser and never uploaded. Convert Thermo .raw first: ThermoRawFileParser -i file.raw -f 2, or msconvert --mzML --zlib.

inputs.name: sequence
inputs.label: Peptide sequence (optional)
inputs.help: Enter the sequence to annotate fragments: PEPTIDE, M[Oxidation], [Acetyl]-..., lowercase = D-residue, (Orn) / [MeL] for non-standard residues, cyclo(...) for head-to-tail rings. Leave empty to browse and measure only.

inputs.name: topology
inputs.label: Topology
inputs.help: Linear peptides give a/b/c and x/y/z series; head-to-tail cyclic peptides give contiguous b/a arcs (and c/z-type arcs in ETD). cyclo(...) in the sequence sets cyclic automatically.

inputs.name: precursorCharge
inputs.label: Precursor charge (0 = auto)
inputs.help: 0 uses the charge inferred from the precursor isotope spacing in the MS2 scans, then the charge written in the file. Thermo converters often write a wrong charge, so set it here when you know it.

inputs.name: activation
inputs.label: Fragmentation
inputs.help: Auto reads the activation from the scan filter string (handles HCD, CID, ETD, EThcD, ETciD, IR-ETD, IRMPD); pick one to override the ion-series preset.

inputs.name: ionTypes
inputs.label: Ion types
inputs.help: Fragment series to annotate. Leave on the preset (follows the fragmentation method) or click chips to choose; cyclic peptides use ring-arc ion types.

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.label: Fragment tolerance
inputs.help: Mass tolerance for assigning peaks. 10 ppm suits Orbitrap and Astral data (5 ppm after recalibration); use ~0.4 Da (switch the unit under Advanced) for ion-trap spectra.

inputs.name: averageTolPpm
inputs.label: Averaging tolerance
inputs.help: When averaging several scans, peaks within this many ppm are merged (intensity-weighted m/z, mean intensity). 10 ppm is a good default for Orbitrap MS2.

inputs.name: losses
inputs.label: Neutral losses (H₂O, NH₃)
inputs.help: Annotate −H₂O (fragments with S, T, E, D) and −NH₃ (R, K, Q, N), up to two combined losses (b−2H₂O, b−H₂O−NH₃) as seen in cyclic peptides.

inputs.name: fixedMods
inputs.label: Fixed modifications
inputs.help: Name@Site, comma separated, e.g. Carbamidomethyl@C or TMT6plex@K+N-term. Leave empty for none.

inputs.name: minFraction
inputs.label: Keep peaks present in ≥
inputs.help: When averaging, a merged peak must appear in at least this fraction of the scans (0.3 = 30 %). Removes random noise; set 0 to keep everything.

inputs.name: minRelIntensity
inputs.label: Intensity threshold
inputs.help: Hide peaks below this percentage of the base peak after averaging (0 keeps all).

inputs.name: toleranceUnit
inputs.label: Tolerance unit
inputs.help: ppm scales with m/z (high-resolution analysers); Da is a fixed window for low-resolution ion-trap data.

inputs.name: maxFragmentCharge
inputs.label: Max fragment charge
inputs.help: Highest fragment charge considered (capped at the precursor charge).

inputs.name: maxLosses
inputs.label: Max losses per fragment
inputs.help: How many neutral losses may combine on one fragment.

inputs.name: modLosses
inputs.label: Modification losses
inputs.help: Characteristic losses from modified residues (−H₃PO₄ from phospho, −CH₄SO from oxidised Met).

inputs.name: adducts
inputs.label: Adduct ions
inputs.help: Also annotate fragments carrying Na⁺, K⁺, NH₄⁺ or Li⁺ instead of one proton.

inputs.name: immonium
inputs.label: Immonium ions
inputs.help: Annotate low-mass immonium ions (residue − CO + H⁺).

inputs.name: precursorIons
inputs.label: Precursor ions
inputs.help: Label the remaining precursor and its neutral losses.

inputs.name: cyclicHydrolysis
inputs.label: b+H₂O ions (cyclic)
inputs.help: Cyclic only: arcs carrying an extra water (ring opened by hydrolysis), typical of depsipeptides.

inputs.name: scrambling
inputs.label: Sequence scrambling (b ions)
inputs.help: Also generate 'scrambled' b-type fragments from macrocyclic b ions that re-close and re-open elsewhere (≥4 residues in rings, ≥5 in linear peptides). Explains extra peaks in large rings (e.g. N-methylated macrocycles) but adds many candidates; flagged as bₖˢ.

inputs.name: sideChainLosses
inputs.label: Side-chain losses
inputs.help: Residue-specific neutral losses: Thr −C₂H₄O, Ser −CH₂O, Asp/Glu −CO₂, Arg −CH₅N₃ and −CH₂N₂, Met −CH₄S, dimethylamide −C₂H₇N.

inputs.name: deisotope
inputs.label: Deisotope (charge from isotopes)
inputs.help: Detect ¹³C isotope envelopes (spacing 1.00336/z) and only accept fragment assignments at the charge the envelope shows. Removes many chance matches of higher-charge ions in dense spectra.

inputs.name: mobilityWindow
inputs.label: Ion-mobility window
inputs.help: For ion-mobility data (timsTOF 1/K0 or drift time arrays in mzML): keep only points inside this range before averaging, e.g. 0.85-1.05. Leave empty to use all points.

outputs.name: peaks
outputs.label: Peak assignments
outputs.help: Every peak with its assignment (automatic or manual), theoretical m/z and error.

outputs.name: averaged
outputs.label: Averaged spectrum
outputs.help: The averaged peak list as MGF.

examples.label: Synthetic demo: gramicidin S + angiotensin II (HCD)
examples.description: Small synthetic mzML (not real data) that exercises scan grouping, averaging and cyclic annotation.

alsoCite.text: Martens L et al. mzML—a community standard for mass spectrometry data. Mol Cell Proteomics 10, R110.000133 (2011).
Teleman J et al. Numerical compression schemes for proteomics mass spectrometry data. Mol Cell Proteomics 13, 1537–1542 (2014).

seo.title: mzML Viewer & MS/MS Annotator (in-browser, cyclic peptides)
seo.metaDescription: Open mzML or MGF files in your browser, average scans, measure peak gaps and annotate linear or cyclic peptide MS/MS spectra. Nothing is uploaded.

faq.a: No. The file is read in slices by a Web Worker inside your browser tab. The page never sends spectra to a server, so it is safe for unpublished data.
Not directly; no browser can read .raw files. Convert them first with ThermoRawFileParser (-f 2 for indexed mzML) or ProteoWizard msconvert, then open the mzML here.

Peaks from all selected scans are pooled and merged within a ppm tolerance using the intensity-weighted m/z; the mean intensity counts missing scans as zero, and peaks seen in fewer than a set fraction of scans (default 30 %) are dropped. Profile scans are centroided first.

faq.q: Why does the charge differ from the one in my file?
faq.a: Thermo converters often write a wrong charge state. The tool infers the charge from the spacing of the residual precursor isotope peaks in the MS2 scans and shows both values; set the charge manually if needed.

maintenance.author: Chase Gibson
maintenance.sourceOrigin: Written for this site; averaging, activation parsing and cyclic ion model follow the owner's cycfrag project (spectra.py, rawmeta.py, fragments.py).

accessibility.notes: Spectrum interaction uses the mouse; the peak table offers the same assignments with the keyboard.
